from datetime import date, timedelta


class LateFeeCalculator:
    """Calculates late fees on invoices for a court finance system.

    Rules:
      - Grace period: 10 days after due_date, no fee.
      - After grace period: 1.5% of outstanding balance per 30-day period,
        prorated by day (i.e. per-day rate = 1.5% / 30).
      - Minimum fee once past grace: $5.
      - Maximum fee: 25% of the original balance (hard cap).
      - Weekends do not count toward the days-late tally (Mon-Fri only).
      - Fees are computed in whole cents (round half up).
      - If balance <= 0, fee is 0 regardless of dates.
    """

    GRACE_DAYS = 10
    MONTHLY_RATE = 0.015
    MIN_FEE_CENTS = 500
    MAX_FEE_FRACTION = 0.25

    def __init__(self, today=None):
        self._today = today or date.today()

    def _weekday_days_between(self, start, end):
        if end <= start:
            return 0
        days = 0
        current = start
        while current < end:
            if current.weekday() < 5:
                days += 1
            current += timedelta(days=1)
        return days

    def compute_fee_cents(self, balance_cents, due_date):
        if balance_cents <= 0:
            return 0
        days_past_due = self._weekday_days_between(due_date, self._today)
        billable_days = days_past_due - self.GRACE_DAYS
        if billable_days <= 0:
            return 0
        per_day_rate = self.MONTHLY_RATE / 30
        raw_fee = balance_cents * per_day_rate * billable_days
        rounded = int(raw_fee + 0.5)
        capped = min(rounded, int(balance_cents * self.MAX_FEE_FRACTION))
        return max(capped, self.MIN_FEE_CENTS)

from datetime import date

import pytest

from late_fee import LateFeeCalculator

# 2024-01-01 is a Monday. All dates below are anchored to it.
DUE = date(2024, 1, 1)


def calc_on(today):
    return LateFeeCalculator(today=today)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constructor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_default_today_is_current_date():
    assert LateFeeCalculator()._today == date.today()


def test_explicit_today_is_kept():
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 3, 3))._today == date(2024, 3, 3)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _weekday_days_between
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "start, end, expected",
    [
        (date(2024, 1, 5), date(2024, 1, 5), 0),   # end == start
        (date(2024, 1, 5), date(2024, 1, 1), 0),   # end < start
        (date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 2), 1),   # Mon -> Tue: one weekday
        (date(2024, 1, 5), date(2024, 1, 8), 1),   # Fri -> Mon: Sat/Sun skipped
        (date(2024, 1, 6), date(2024, 1, 8), 0),   # Sat -> Mon: nothing counted
        (date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 8), 5),   # full week
        (date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 15), 10),  # two full weeks
    ],
)
def test_weekday_days_between(start, end, expected):
    assert calc_on(end)._weekday_days_between(start, end) == expected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# compute_fee_cents: early exits
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("balance", [0, -1, -100_000])
def test_non_positive_balance_is_zero_even_when_very_late(balance):
    assert calc_on(date(2030, 1, 1)).compute_fee_cents(balance, DUE) == 0


def test_today_before_due_date_is_zero():
    assert calc_on(date(2023, 12, 1)).compute_fee_cents(100_000, DUE) == 0


def test_today_equals_due_date_is_zero():
    assert calc_on(DUE).compute_fee_cents(100_000, DUE) == 0


def test_last_day_of_grace_period_is_zero():
    # Jan 1..Jan 12 = exactly 10 weekdays -> billable_days == 0
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 15)).compute_fee_cents(100_000, DUE) == 0


def test_weekend_after_grace_does_not_start_billing():
    # Sat Jan 13 / Sun Jan 14: still only 10 weekdays elapsed
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 13)).compute_fee_cents(100_000, DUE) == 0
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 14)).compute_fee_cents(100_000, DUE) == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# compute_fee_cents: proration, rounding, min, max
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_first_billable_day_prorated():
    # 11 weekdays -> 1 billable day; $20,000 * 0.05% = $10.00
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 16)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 1000


def test_multiple_billable_days_prorated():
    # Jan 1 .. Jan 26 (Fri) = 19 weekdays -> 9 billable; $20,000 * 0.05% * 9 = $90.00
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 26)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 9000


def test_weekend_days_after_grace_are_not_billed():
    # Sat Jan 20, Sun Jan 21 and Mon Jan 22 all see 15 weekdays -> 5 billable
    sat = calc_on(date(2024, 1, 20)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE)
    sun = calc_on(date(2024, 1, 21)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE)
    mon = calc_on(date(2024, 1, 22)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE)
    assert sat == sun == mon == 5000


def test_rounds_half_up_to_whole_cents():
    # $12,345 * 0.05% * 1 = 617.25 -> 617 ; * 3 = 1851.75 -> 1852
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 16)).compute_fee_cents(1_234_500, DUE) == 617
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 18)).compute_fee_cents(1_234_500, DUE) == 1852


def test_minimum_fee_applies_when_prorated_fee_is_small():
    # $100 * 0.05% * 1 = 5 cents -> floored up to $5.00
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 16)).compute_fee_cents(10_000, DUE) == 500


def test_fee_just_above_minimum_is_not_clamped():
    # $10,020 * 0.05% * 1 = 501 cents
    assert calc_on(date(2024, 1, 16)).compute_fee_cents(1_002_000, DUE) == 501


def test_maximum_fee_caps_at_25_percent_of_balance():
    # 3 years late: raw fee far exceeds 25% of $100
    assert calc_on(date(2027, 1, 1)).compute_fee_cents(10_000, DUE) == 2500


def test_cap_uses_truncated_integer_cents():
    # 25% of 10_003 cents = 2500.75 -> int() truncates to 2500
    assert calc_on(date(2027, 1, 1)).compute_fee_cents(10_003, DUE) == 2500


def test_minimum_fee_wins_over_cap_for_tiny_balances():
    # Documents current behaviour: max(min(raw, cap), MIN) lets the $5 minimum
    # exceed the 25% cap when the balance is under $20.
    assert calc_on(date(2027, 1, 1)).compute_fee_cents(1_000, DUE) == 500

Notes

  • All dates are anchored to Monday, 2024-01-01, so weekday arithmetic in the comments can be checked by hand. Ten weekdays after Jan 1 land on Jan 15 (Monday), which is the last zero-fee day.
  • The class counts weekdays from due_date inclusive to today exclusive. The test for Sat Jan 20, Sun Jan 21 and Mon Jan 22 all returning the same fee pins down that weekends add nothing.
  • Expected values were computed by hand and confirmed against the implementation: e.g. $12,345 at 0.05%/day for 3 days is 1851.75 cents, which rounds half-up to 1852.
  • test_minimum_fee_wins_over_cap_for_tiny_balances documents a real quirk: because the code applies max(..., MIN_FEE) after the cap, a $10 balance can carry a $5 fee even though the docstring calls 25% a "hard cap". If that is a bug, this is the test to flip.
  • Run with pytest --cov=late_fee --cov-branch test_late_fee.py. Every conditional in the module has both arms exercised, so branch coverage is 100%.
